# Two Emissions Tracks in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector through different mechanisms. In its sulfur dioxide system, an allowance represents permission to emit one ton under an aggregate cap, with allowances available for trading.

The sulfur dioxide program expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.

Nitrogen oxides regulation followed a separate track. For certain coal-fired units, it began in 1996 and used a rate-based approach, without a cap or allowance trading. The program therefore had distinct mechanisms and timelines for its two pollutants.
